You know what we are building. Take the whole codebase and make a testing CSV file of how it is going to be for different users. It should be a really really really detailed user testing CSV file with each thing tested one by one, each user's walkthrough, and all of that. Those things are there.

Once you have generated a really detailed one, call a subagent to test all those walkthroughs, each testing instance, and all of those things. Once that is done as well, take note of all the problems, the things that partially passed, the things which did not pass, the things which did not work, the UI/UX failure, and the things which are not clear for the user. Take note of all of that in a really detailed way.

The task of this agent would be to think from a user perspective, even for things which are not that clear or not that good-looking as per UI or UX, and then create the list of all the findings that you could find. To do that first make a list of all the things to test and then call a subagent to do the check on it like a user would do it if you have access to my browser. If you want anything you can ask for it as well and you can run the application and test it from there.

Once that is done, from there create a list of things. Not only the testing but also have in mind to tell the subagent to also see things which are not very clear, which do not look that UI or UX friendly, which look shit, or which look too cluttered and could be fixed. At the end give me the list of things that need to be fixed. 

if any question ask me
I'll map the product first so the CSV covers what's actually there.

2	
3	## Bounded investigation acceptance
4	
5	`npx playwright test --config e2e/review-investigation.config.ts` runs the installed Next/Workflow runtime with the unchanged analysis form/routes, dispatcher, bounded controller, deterministic reader, receipt persistence, synthesis and freshness code. Its local synthetic HTTP database/model boundaries use no Supabase auth, public DDL, financial account or paid provider. The synthetic owner cookie exists only in the ignored harness app; it does not alter production authentication.
6	
7	The gate checks chosen question/focus/dates/planning through UI dispatch and reload, material decline drill-down, retained checkpoint-response loss and durable retry, support exhaustion, unavailable follow-ups, an actual read deadline with zero synthesis transport calls, source fingerprint change with unchanged historical output, and Stop settling the actual synthesis fetch before suppressing publication. Exact fixture IDs are deleted in `finally`; Next runs in `.qa/mne019-runtime`, and the harness stops its Windows Next process tree on shutdown. Run only with the shared heavy/browser slot released, ports3040/3041 free, and Playwright Chromium installed. These prepared tests require execution; syntax/lint checks are not runtime acceptance. Real SQL ownership/reservation races, Supabase authentication and deployed acceptance remain separate gates.
8	
9	## Financial-review recovery acceptance
10	
11	`npx playwright test --config e2e/review-runtime.config.ts` compiles the actual financial-review workflow, dispatcher, recovery route and instrumentation with the installed Next/Workflow runtime. Its synthetic HTTP database/provider boundaries use no bank records or provider account. The interruption case kills the actual Next process tree during provider work, restarts against the same persisted local Workflow world, and requires the same run identity and one publication. `node supabase/tests/run-review-runtime.mjs` separately exercises actual Postgres functions/roles and lock races in an exactly removed disposable schema; it does not apply public migrations.
12	
13	The review recovery cron is configured daily at 01:00 UTC, independently of summary preferences, using `CRON_SECRET`. Each invocation examines the oldest 25 active reviews; observed active jobs move behind other candidates even after a runtime error when the database remains usable through a checked timestamp update. The 24-hour dispatch deadline is a business policy, checked at the next successful reconciliation, rather than a Workflow execution timeout. Normal retries remain active before that deadline. After the deadline, recovery awaits runtime cancellation and confirmed terminal status before failing an active application job. Missing runtime records receive the same 24-hour receipt grace. Unacknowledged claims expire 24 hours after creation through a conditional update that cannot overwrite a concurrent elected run or publication; late workers must still register before useful work. Transport/cleanup/cancel errors remain recoverable and produce a 503 cron response. There is no automatic replacement of an acknowledged run.
14	
15	Daily scheduling is compatible with Vercel Hobby. For up to 25 eligible jobs and healthy services, deadline convergence occurs at the next daily invocation (about 24 hours plus the cadence and platform scheduling delay); a backlog takes further invocations. Persistent service failures are reported and cannot guarantee a wall-clock bound. Actual deployed cron registration, credentials, invocations and Vercel durable-queue behavior require separate deployment acceptance; local runtime/SQL tests do not establish them.
16	
17	## Repository release gates
18	
19	`npx playwright test --config e2e/review-runtime.config.ts --grep 'Stop aborts'` runs the installed Next/Workflow engine and actual AI SDK/OpenAI HTTP transport against a controlled local provider. Stop is observed through bounded database polling every 500 ms (each read has a 2 s timeout), aborts the active request, and persists acknowledgment only after the application transport settles. Runtime cancellation follows that acknowledgment. No provider account or financial records are used. This does not establish deletion of data a remote provider already received or provider-side termination.
20	
21	`e2e/provider-stop.gated.spec.ts` requires deployed migration 202610060013 and real disposable Supabase authentication. It checks owned Stop/reload requested versus acknowledged state, an explicitly unconfirmed termination receipt, late-publication suppression, completed report retention and unchanged intentional correction/history. Its worker acknowledgment is a controlled service receipt; the separate installed-runtime HTTP test establishes real transport abort. Recovery allows a canceled runtime's running step time to acknowledge, then uses `cancellation_unconfirmed` for stale steps rather than claiming termination. Runtime/step lookup failures remain recoverable, and missing cancellation timestamps use the existing 24-hour deadline. Actual hosted Workflow/provider cancellation remains a separate deployment check.
22	
23	Run `npm run acceptance:fast` (unit tests, lint, build), then `npm run acceptance:required` (rollback-only fresh/upgrade SQL regressions, unit tests with live DB balance parity, and the deterministic browser suite with one worker). Both commands must pass for local release acceptance. Fast validation alone permits the default live DB test skip and is not release evidence.
24	
25	The required tier fails on absent prerequisites, failed commands, empty reports, any unit/browser skip, or flaky browser results. It also requires the latest fast result to pass on a clean checkout and match the current commit and `.next/BUILD_ID`; rerun `npm run acceptance:fast` after any commit, uncommitted change or replacement build. Configure `.env` with `SUPABASE_DB_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`; supply `E2E_STORAGE_STATE` (or `e2e/.auth.json`) for an empty disposable synthetic workspace. Install Playwright Chromium and apply the repository migration head through your normal reviewed deployment process before browser acceptance. Stop any existing port3000 server before the fast build; stop any port3000 server before the required tier too: it starts the verified production build with `npm start`, without HMR, existing-server reuse or a live provider key. `E2E_PRODUCTION_BUILD=1` selects that production server for direct Playwright runs; ordinary runs retain the development server.
26	
27	Each invocation writes an ignored `.qa/acceptance-<tier>-<timestamp>/result.json` with tested commit, worktree-dirty flag, migration filename head, command outcomes, production build ID and local environment label. Detailed logs, reports and browser artifacts stay in that ignored directory because they may contain identifying evidence. Run against a clean committed checkout for revision-bound evidence; dirty results explicitly describe an uncommitted tree. No credentials or auth contents are included in the summary.
28	
29	Fresh application schema replay and SQL fixtures run in a disposable schema and roll back before upgrading the configured database inside a separate rollback-only transaction. Upgrade failure does not negate the separately logged fresh pass. Schema changed outside `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` can make a pending migration fail; reconcile that discrepancy through the normal reviewed database process, never skip or mark SQL applied merely to turn this gate green. The harness neither applies migrations permanently nor rewrites migration history.
30	
31	Actual provider quality/cancellation evaluation is a separate optional, explicitly budgeted tier, not run by either command. The existing `core-journey.gated.spec.ts` invokes the live provider and is explicitly excluded from the required tier and recorded in its summary; run that journey separately when provider evaluation is authorized. Browser AI mocks remain deterministic contracts. Local gates do not establish deployed revision/health/auth/journey or Vercel administration acceptance; record those separately. New issue-specific regression journeys remain necessary where existing tests do not cover their failures.
32	
33	Use `npm run test:e2e -- --workers=1 --output=.qa/final-e2e-results` with the configured local app and applied migrations. The config reads `.env`; it reuses a running port3000 server. Stop that server before building so build/dev do not write the same `.next` directory.

35	Authenticated specs require `E2E_STORAGE_STATE` pointing at an ignored Playwright storage state, or `e2e/.auth.json`. Other gated specs create their own disposable users and require `SUPABASE_DB_URL`, the public Supabase variables and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`. No production authentication bypass is used and no test emails are sent. Never commit credentials, auth state, private statements or detailed private evidence. A skipped required authenticated spec is not a pass.
36	
37	Use an empty disposable workspace for the full suite: the core journey independently expects its initial two ledger entries. Run with one worker because several authenticated specs mutate the same supplied workspace/preferences. Specs that create users remove their exact fixtures in `finally`; ignored `.qa` recovery journals retain IDs if interrupted. Remove only those recorded QA records and storage objects after acceptance.

42	- `core-journey.gated.spec.ts` uses real auth, confirmation/import workflow, ledger, chat and goals; file interpretation/manual analysis start are explicitly mocked. 47	- `reviewed-balances.gated.spec.ts` requires migration `202610060001`; it covers explicit timestamp/date-only posted activity review, conservative unconfirmed balances, later postings and retained undo history. A rollback-only migration test cannot enable this browser gate.

1	# Moneo
2	
3	Moneo is a personal finance workspace for importing transactions, tracking accounts, planning spending, and exploring your finances with AI. It is a Next.js and TypeScript app backed by Supabase.
4	
5	## Run locally
6	
7	1. Install dependencies: `npm ci`
8	2. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and add your Supabase URL and publishable key. Add `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` for import and analysis workflows, and `OPENAI_API_KEY` for AI features (models per agent are set in Settings).
9	3. Apply the SQL files in `supabase/migrations/` to your Supabase project in filename order. Configure Supabase email sign-in with `http://localhost:3000/auth/callback` as an allowed redirect URL.
10	4. Start the app: `npm run dev`, then open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000).
11	5. Sign in: during `npm run dev` on localhost, type your email and click **Sign in instantly (local dev)**. It needs `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, sends no email, and is disabled in production builds. The normal email link also works, but must be opened in the same browser that requested it.
12	
13	Without Supabase keys, the home page shows a setup message. Keep `.env` private; it is git-ignored.
14	
15	If `npm run dev` says another server is already running, stop the old one (the message prints its PID, e.g. `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` on Windows) and start again.
16	
17	## Deploy to Vercel
18	
19	Set the environment variables from `.env.example` in Vercel, using your deployed website origin for `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` (for example, `https://your-moneo.vercel.app`).
20	
21	In the same Supabase project used by Vercel, open **Authentication → URL Configuration**:
22	
23	1. Set **Site URL** to your deployed website origin.
24	2. Add the exact deployed callback URL to **Redirect URLs**, for example `https://your-moneo.vercel.app/auth/callback`. Keep `http://localhost:3000/auth/callback` for local development. Add each additional domain you use for sign-in explicitly.
25	3. Under **Authentication → Email Templates**, ensure **Confirm signup** and **Magic Link** use `{{ .ConfirmationURL }}` as their sign-in link, without a hardcoded localhost URL.
26	
27	The login page supplies the current website's `/auth/callback` as `emailRedirectTo`. Supabase must allow that exact URL or it falls back to **Site URL**, which defaults to localhost. Changing `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` alone does not change Supabase's authentication settings. See [Supabase redirect troubleshooting](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/troubleshooting/why-am-i-being-redirected-to-the-wrong-url-when-using-auth-redirectto-option-_vqIeO).
28	
29	After saving the settings, request a new sign-in email from the deployed website and open it in the same browser used to request it. Previously sent emails retain their original URLs.
30	
31	## Connect your bank (optional)
32	
33	Moneo can sync booked transactions and balances from EU banks (for example Revolut and Commerzbank) through [Enable Banking](https://enablebanking.com). Its restricted mode is free for personal use and covers the accounts you link yourself. Each sync is written as an ordinary import, so it shows in import history and can be reviewed and undone.

35	1. Sign up at the [Enable Banking control panel](https://enablebanking.com/cp/) and create a new application in the **Production** environment. A new production app runs in restricted mode, which limits it to linked accounts.
